prompt:
Hi, I'm the data lead for our SmartFab manufacturing plant. We have pressure sensor readings from two groups of sensors — Group A (8 sensors) and Group B (6 sensors) — each recorded over 120 time steps. The raw CSVs are at `plant_data/line_A/raw/sensor_group_A.csv` and `plant_data/line_B/raw/sensor_group_B.csv`.

I need two things delivered as NumPy binary files:

1. **`distance_matrix.npy`** — A matrix capturing how dissimilar each sensor in Group A is from each sensor in Group B (one number per pair, so 8×6 values). Please don't use any slow row-by-row loops — our pipeline benchmarks this step.

2. **`dominant_eigenvalues.npy`** — From that distance matrix, derive a square cross-product matrix (your choice of which one makes sense), compute its characteristic frequency modes, keep only the ones that are real-valued and positive (discard the rest), and save them in the most memory-compact floating-point format that still preserves the values adequately.

Just drop both `.npy` files anywhere in the workspace. No report needed.
